name: Planning Which Tools to Use
gist: Papers about helping agents decide which tools to call in the right order, like planning a multi-step recipe before you start cooking.
explain: This cluster focuses on a specific problem: agents have to decide not just which tool to call right now, but which sequence of tools will actually solve the problem. Think of planning as making a recipe before you cook. If you want to make a cake, you need eggs, flour, sugar, butter — you gather them in some order, you prepare your equipment, you mix things in a specific sequence, then bake. If you did everything in the wrong order, you would ruin it. AI agents face the same challenge when solving problems with tools: calling a database query before knowing what question to ask is wasted. Running a spell-checker before you have written the text is pointless. The papers here focus on teaching agents to figure out the right sequence.

Planning is hard because the space of possible sequences is huge. With just ten tools, there are trillions of ways to arrange them. The agent can't try all of them. Also, the right sequence depends on the specific problem — what works for one question might be terrible for another. An agent needs to learn to recognize the shape of a problem and know which sequence of tools works for that shape. Plus, when the agent calls a tool and gets a result, it might need to replan — the result might be unexpected and require a different next step than it originally planned.

Researchers tackle this by building planning systems that reason about dependencies and subgoals. Some papers focus on learning from demonstrations — showing the agent examples of correct tool sequences and letting it generalize, so the agent learns patterns without having to discover them from scratch. Others use search algorithms that explore promising sequences without trying all of them, which saves time by pruning obviously bad paths. Some agents build a model of what each tool does and reason backwards from the goal ('I want this answer; what tool produces that?') to figure out what to call and in what order, because working backwards from the end state often makes the dependencies clearer. The goal is agents that can take a new problem, figure out a reasonable plan, and then execute it.

papers.title: DRIFT: Decompose, Retrieve, Illustrate, then Formalize Theorems
papers.contribution: DRIFT consistently improves premise retrieval nearly doubling F1 score compared to DPR baseline on ProofNet with strong performance on out-of-distribution ConNF benchmark.

papers.title: DreamPhase: Offline Imagination and Uncertainty-Guided Planning for Large-Language-Model Agents
papers.contribution: DreamPhase reduces average API calls from 40 to less than 10 per episode on WebShop (4x reduction) while improving sample efficiency, safety, and cost.

papers.title: Emergent Discrete Controller Modules for Symbolic Planning in Transformers
papers.contribution: Achieves strong length generalization on algorithmic benchmarks with 20-40 point improvements in longest-length accuracy over baselines.

papers.title: From Assumptions to Actions: Turning LLM Reasoning into Uncertainty-Aware Planning for Embodied Agents
papers.contribution: Outperforms communication-centric baselines in success rate and task efficiency across C-WAH and TDW-MAT benchmarks with comparable token usage on three LLM backbones.

papers.title: MARS: Modular Agent with Reflective Search for Automated AI Research
papers.contribution: MARS achieves state-of-the-art performance on MLE-Bench, with 63% of utilized lessons originating from cross-branch transfer, demonstrating effective insight generalization.

papers.title: Simulation to Rules: A Dual-VLM Framework for Formal Visual Planning
papers.contribution: VLMFP autonomously generates both problem and domain PDDL files with generalization across instances, appearances, and rules without human domain engineering.

papers.title: ToolTree: Efficient LLM Tool Planning via Dual-Feedback Monte Carlo Tree Search and Bidirectional Pruning
papers.contribution: ToolTree achieves an average 10% gain over state-of-the-art planning methods while maintaining highest efficiency across open-set and closed-set tool planning benchmarks.

papers.title: ToolWeaver: Weaving Collaborative Semantics for Scalable Tool Use in Large Language Models
papers.contribution: Reduces vocabulary expansion from linear to logarithmic in tool count and improves generalization through dense co-occurrence of shared tool codes.

papers.title: $R^3$DAO: Reactive Recovery and Reconstruction for Long-horizon Data Agent Orchestration
papers.contribution: Achieves 77.36% improvement in success rate over advanced R&D-Agent on MLE-bench while compressing average execution time.

papers.title: A Systematic Study of Behavioral Cloning for Scientific Data Annotation
papers.contribution: Shows larger models are more data-efficient; multi-task pretraining enables efficient fine-tuning; models learn mistake representation generalizing across tasks.

papers.title: AdverMCTS: Combating Pseudo-Correctness in Code Generation via Adversarial Monte Carlo Tree Search
papers.contribution: Significantly outperforms baselines by reducing false positive rates and forcing generalization beyond initial test constraints.

papers.title: Agent JIT Compilation for Latency-Optimizing Web Agent Planning and Scheduling
papers.contribution: Achieves 10.4x speedup and 28% higher accuracy over Browser-Use, with 2.4x speedup and 9% over OpenAI CUA.

papers.title: AgentXRay: White-Boxing Agentic Systems via Workflow Reconstruction
papers.contribution: AgentXRay produces editable white-box workflows matching target outputs without model parameters, achieving higher proxy similarity and reduced token consumption compared to unpruned search.

papers.title: Analytica: Soft Propositional Reasoning for Robust and Scalable LLM-Driven Analysis
papers.contribution: Analytica improves accuracy by 15.84% on average over diverse base models on economic, financial, and political forecasting tasks, achieving 71.06% accuracy with lowest variance.

papers.title: Closing the Loop: Universal Repository Representation with RPG-Encoder
papers.contribution: Achieves 93.7% Acc@5 on SWE-bench Verified (10% better than baselines), 98.5% reconstruction coverage on RepoCraft, enabling fine-grained localization in complex codebases.

papers.title: CoDA: Agentic Systems for Collaborative Data Visualization
papers.contribution: CoDA achieves substantial gains, outperforming baselines by up to 41.5% through integrated, collaborative agentic workflows.

papers.title: CoPE: A Framework for Optimizing Coordination between Planning and Execution in LLM-based Agents
papers.contribution: CoPE substantially improves agent coordination and outperforms baselines on benchmarks with long-horizon multi-step tasks.

papers.title: Darwinian Memory: A Training-Free Self-Regulating Memory System for GUI Agent Evolution
papers.contribution: Boosts general-purpose MLLMs without training, achieving average gains of 18.0% in success rate and 33.9% in execution stability on real-world multi-app tasks.

papers.title: Discovering Hierarchical Software Engineering Agents via Bandit Optimization
papers.contribution: Ranks 2nd on SWE-bench-Live with 36B model, surpassing larger systems like GPT-4 and Claude, providing first evidence hierarchical multi-agent systems improve generalization.

papers.title: Enhancing Agentic Search via Data Synthesis on Hierarchical Constraint Satisfaction
papers.contribution: First publicly released framework for agentic search data synthesis with open-source code and curated datasets, substantially improving performance on diverse information-seeking benchmarks.

papers.title: EvoC2F: Compiling Tool Orchestration for Efficient and Evolvable LLM Agents
papers.contribution: EvoC2F outperforms existing methods by reducing latency while establishing soundness guarantees, providing a robust foundation for building reliable, evolving autonomous agents.

papers.title: FaSTA*: Fast-Slow Toolpath Agent with Subroutine Mining for Efficient Multi-turn Image Editing
papers.contribution: FaSTA* achieves significant computational efficiency gains while remaining competitive with state-of-the-art image editing baselines by reusing symbolic subroutines and triggering A* only for novel tasks.

papers.title: FlowMAP: Flow Matching for Generalizable Agent Planning
papers.contribution: Consistently outperforms strong baselines with improved planning generalization across diverse benchmarks.

papers.title: From Winning to Understanding: A Diagnostic Long-Horizon RTS Benchmark for LLMs
papers.contribution: Provides reproducible diagnostic testbed identifying long-horizon failure modes through economy/combat/visibility metrics.

papers.title: Helmsman: Autonomous Synthesis of Federated Learning Systems via Collaborative LLM Agents
papers.contribution: Generates FL solutions competitive with and often superior to established baselines on AgentFL-Bench (16 diverse tasks), advancing automated engineering of decentralized AI systems.

papers.title: Hierarchical Procedural Meta-Reasoning for Generalizable Multimodal Agents
papers.contribution: Enables robust generalization across tasks, applications, interface versions, and multi-app workflows on challenging Android benchmarks.

papers.title: LLM2Fx-Tools: Tool Calling for Music Post-Production
papers.contribution: Enables inference of Fx-chains and parameters from unprocessed and processed audio pairs, with application to style transfer and interpretable music production.

papers.title: LightWM: Training-Free Hierarchical Working Memory for Small Language Model Agents
papers.contribution: Achieve 0.910 success on ALFWorld valid_unseen with Qwen3-4B, whereas representative baselines remain below 0.320.

papers.title: MAS-Architect: Declarative Multi-Agent System Design via Separation of Concerns
papers.contribution: Achieves 78.7% average accuracy across benchmarks with only 2,533 tokens per query, surpassing state-of-the-art while substantially lowering token usage; exhibits emergent collaboration patterns.

papers.title: MINT: Minimal Information Neuro-Symbolic Tree for Objective-Driven Knowledge-Gap Reasoning and Active Elicitation
papers.contribution: MINT-based planning attains near-expert returns by issuing limited questions per task while achieving significantly improved rewards and success rates across benchmarks.

papers.title: MM-DeepResearch: A Simple and Effective Multimodal Agentic Search Baseline
papers.contribution: Develops a powerful multimodal deep research agent showing superiority across benchmarks through offline training and cross-modal information synthesis.

papers.title: NaviAgent: Graph‑Driven Bilevel Planning for Scalable Tool Orchestration
papers.contribution: NaviAgent achieves consistent improvements in task success rate with TWNM yielding an average gain of 13.1 points on complex tasks and 4.3-12.0 points on real APIs.

papers.title: OpenSage: Self-programming Agent Generation Engine
papers.contribution: OpenSage is the first ADK that shifts from human-centered to AI-centered agent design, demonstrating advantages across three benchmarks with various backbone models.

papers.title: Operator Theory-Driven Autoformulation of MDPs for Control of Queueing Systems
papers.contribution: Proves universal three-level operator-graph topology that significantly shrinks MDP formulation search space, enabling practical autoformulation for queueing systems.

papers.title: Order Matters: Unveiling the Hidden Impact of Macro Placement Sequences via Proxy-Guided LLM Evolution
papers.contribution: Reduces wirelength by 34.04% versus WireMask-EA and 14.08% versus state-of-the-art EGPlace on ISPD 2005 benchmarks.

papers.title: RE-TRAC: REcursive TRAjectory Compression for Deep Search Agents
papers.contribution: Re-TRAC consistently outperforms ReAct by 15-20% on BrowseComp with frontier LLMs, shows monotonic reduction in tool calls and token usage across rounds, and achieves state-of-the-art performance at comparable scales when combined with supervised fine-tuning.

papers.title: RPG: A Repository Planning Graph for Unified and Scalable Codebase Generation
papers.contribution: On RepoCraft benchmark, produces 3.9x larger code than strongest baseline with 81.5% coverage and 69.7% test accuracy; generates approximately 36K Code Lines and 445K Code Tokens.

papers.title: ReCAPA: Hierarchical Predictive Correction to Mitigate Cascading Failures
papers.contribution: Achieves competitive results on VisualAgentBench, MineDojo, and MAP-THOR, outperforming strong LLM baselines with two new metrics quantifying error propagation.

papers.title: Real-Time Reasoning Agents in Evolving Environments
papers.contribution: AgileThinker consistently outperforms single-paradigm agents as task difficulty and time pressure rise.

papers.title: SciNav: A Principled Agent Framework for Scientific Coding Tasks
papers.contribution: The framework enables more effective solution exploration for scientific coding tasks under constrained search budgets.

papers.title: Self-CriTeach: LLM Self-Teaching and Self-Critiquing for Improving Robotic Planning via Automated Domain Generation
papers.contribution: Achieve higher planning success, stronger cross-task generalization, reduced inference cost, and resistance to imperfect logical states.

papers.title: Strategic Planning and Rationalizing on Trees Make LLMs Better Debaters
papers.contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art multi-agent debate with +15.6% improvement in stage-level persuasiveness (DeepSeek) and +10% debate-level opinion shift, better aligning with human expert strategies.

papers.title: Talk, Judge, Cooperate: Gossip-Driven Indirect Reciprocity in Self-Interested LLM Agents
papers.contribution: Stronger reasoning capabilities lead to incentive-aligned cooperation, with ALIGN improving indirect reciprocity and resisting malicious entrants.

papers.title: Towards Professional-Grade Financial Agents: Benchmarking, Tooling, and Structured Reasoning
papers.contribution: ProFinAgent achieves 49.81% performance gain over baselines with 47.1% reduction in inference latency across professional finance reasoning tasks.

papers.title: Towards Whole-corpus Reconstruction of Heterogeneous RAG Knowledge Bases
papers.contribution: GeoEx significantly outperforms baselines in extraction coverage and query efficiency across eight diverse domains and multiple retrievers/LLMs.

papers.title: WebWeaver: Structuring Web-Scale Evidence with Dynamic Outlines for Open-Ended Deep Research
papers.contribution: WebWeaver establishes state-of-the-art performance across DeepResearch Bench, DeepConsult, and DeepResearchGym benchmarks.

papers.title: When AI Agents Compete for Jobs: Strategic Capabilities and Economic Dynamics of AI Labour Markets
papers.contribution: Demonstrates that agents with metacognition, competitive awareness, and strategic planning consistently achieve higher profits and market share than competing agents.

papers.title: WorldTravel: A Realistic Multimodal Travel-Planning Benchmark with Tightly Coupled Constraints
papers.contribution: Reveal severe performance collapse in frontier models (GPT-5.2 achieves 28.0% feasibility in text, 3.4% in multimodal) and identify Planning Horizon threshold at ~10 constraints.
